analysis: What changed vs the 7:00 AM brief: the selloff deepened rather than stabilized. Intel went from ~-25% at the open to ~-28% to -30% in morning trading, near its worst session since 1974, and the Dow gave back its flat open to trade -0.3% to -0.7%, so the rotation story is weakening at the margin even though energy (Exxon/Chevron refining beats) and health care still offset. The Nasdaq's -2.26% open became -2.3% to -2.5% mid-morning, and the breadth picture is mixed by snapshot time (SKN Russell +1.01% vs IBD early-trade small caps -0.9%), so do not read small caps as a clean offset yet. Signal: this remains a repricing of AI economics on three fronts at once — cash burn (Amazon -$42.4B FCF, Alphabet -$9.07B), demand warnings (Intel PCs into H1 2027), and AI disruption of traffic (Reddit -25% on Google AI search, with analyst downgrades confirming the story). Noise: the month-end optics and the $300B Amazon+Intel value-loss headline will dominate, but the S&P is still +0.7% for October and Chicago PMI (55.3, below 56.1 forecast, still expanding) is not a macro driver here. The next test is the Fed speakers at noon ET and whether the close holds the Nasdaq's month-end loss near its current level.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Mid-morning: the tech selloff deepened from the open — Nasdaq -2.3% to -2.5%, S&P 500 -1.2% to -1.5%, Dow -0.3% to -0.7% in morning snapshots (IBD early trade; Investopedia recent trading; SKN), after the open printed Nasdaq -2.26% to 25,592.5, S&P -1.16% to 7,631.07 and Dow +0.08% to 52,383.9.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Dow giving back its flat open shows the rotation is fading at the margin — the selloff is still tech-led, but it is no longer leaving the broad market untouched.

headlines.headline: Intel's plunge worsened to about -28% to -30% in morning trading (AP via EL7/Investopedia), nearing its worst session since 1974, after the Q4 guide ($15-16B revenue, ~$0.25 EPS) trailed consensus; Bank of America downgraded Intel to Neutral from Buy and cut its target to $100 from $145.
headlines.why_it_matters: A 25% premarket drop becoming a ~30% regular-session drop means the guide, not the Q3 beat, is doing all the pricing — and it keeps dragging the whole chip complex with it.

headlines.headline: Amazon still down about 7% in morning trading after Q3 revenue $201.9B vs ~$202.2B expected and EPS $1.89 vs ~$1.97 expected; trailing-12-month free cash flow swung to -$42.4B from +$14.8B a year earlier, 2026 cash capex held at ~$220B with 2027 set higher, and CEO Andy Jassy said AWS growth should exceed 40% in 2027 and 2028.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even a faster AWS growth promise for 2027-28 is not offsetting the cash line today — the market is still grading AI spenders on free cash flow first.

headlines.headline: Chip and PC spillover: AMD and Arm each down more than 10% in morning trading (IBD), Nvidia down about 3%, Broadcom down about 3.9%, SanDisk down nearly 9% premarket despite beating Q1 forecasts, and HP down over 8% and Dell over 10% premarket on Intel's PC warning.
headlines.why_it_matters: Intel's PC-demand and memory-shortage warning is now a sector read — even a SanDisk beat could not escape it, which is how a single guide becomes a complex-wide repricing.

headlines.headline: Reddit crashed 25% in morning trading (IBD), extending a seven-day losing streak, after warning daily active uniques could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 from ~130 million (which missed the 134 million estimate) as Google AI search referrals fell by more than one million a week on average in October; Q3 EPS $1.40 beat $1.33 and revenue $895M beat $875M (FactSet), but Q4 revenue guidance of $1.00-1.03B trails the ~$1.05B consensus, and BofA and Citizens downgraded while Guggenheim and Needham kept Buy ratings with lower targets.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat that still crashes 25% shows the traffic story now outweighs the quarter — and the analyst split (downgrades vs Buy-with-lower-targets) marks this as a debate about AI-search disruption, not a one-day flush.

headlines.headline: Megacap morning snapshot (MarketBeat compare): Apple -0.2%, Alphabet -0.9%, Meta -1.0%, Microsoft -1.5%, Nvidia -2.6%, Tesla -2.9%; IBD separately notes Tesla was down about 3% Friday morning yet up about 5% for the week — the week's best Magnificent Seven performer — while Alphabet slipped another ~1% after Thursday's ~13% plunge that erased roughly $500B in market value.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla holding up for the week while its peers fall shows the selloff is selective, not indiscriminate — investors are still distinguishing earnings stories inside the Mag Seven.

headlines.headline: Energy offset confirmed by Reuters: ExxonMobil and Chevron both beat Q3 profit expectations on a refining surge — Exxon adjusted EPS $4.23, Chevron $5.28 — with Exxon earning more from refining than upstream for the first time in at least six years and Chevron's downstream earnings at a six-year-plus high; both shares rose about 2% in early trading, and Exxon cut debt by $8B in Q3.
headlines.why_it_matters: Refining margins, lifted by Hormuz disruption and refinery attacks, are the morning's real offset — energy strength is earnings-driven, not just an oil-price bounce.

headlines.headline: Macro: October Chicago PMI came in at 55.3, below the 56.1 forecast and down from 58.8 in September — still in expansion territory above 50, but cooling.
headlines.why_it_matters: A softer-but-still-expanding PMI does not explain a tech selloff and does not change the Fed-speaker read later today — it keeps this an earnings story, not a macro one.

headlines.headline: Month-end context carried forward: today is the final session of October — the Dow is up 2.7% for the month and the S&P 500 up 0.7%, while the Nasdaq is down 2.7% and set to break a two-month winning streak; Amazon and Intel together are set to shed about $300 billion in market value if opening losses hold.
headlines.why_it_matters: The month-end tape still frames today as a tech-complex reset inside an otherwise positive month for the broad market — context against reading it as a market-wide rout.
